name: Closed-form and tabulated references for the structural (static) part: section properties, cantilever moments/deflections, centrifugal stress

experiments.validates: calculation.Calculator.get_crossection_data (solid: blade_design 0; hollow: blade_design 1 with blade_thickness = wall_m), bending_inertia.calculate_bending_inertia_2 / calculate_centroid / generate_hollow_foil; the extreme-fibre distances used for stress_norm / stress_tang
experiments.conditions: one row per section; feed airfoil_file scaled by c_m (the .dat files are unit chord except where noted), rotated by theta_deg (counter-clockwise in the x-to-TE / y-to-suction-side frame; formulas for other frames in the CSV header); compare A, Ix, Iy (and Ixy) within tolerance_rel
experiments.source: exact geometry (NACA 4-digit definition, circle, ellipse, Chen et al. 2010 Fig. 6) integrated independently (extraction/make_reference.py, cross-checked by XFOIL BEND and by closed-form integrals); tabulated rows from Chen, Yu & Capellaro 2010 Tables I and IV; Drela's rule-of-thumb rows
experiments.uncertainty: exact rows: < 1e-8 numerical (conv_rel); tabulated Chen rows: 4 significant digits; Drela rule: ~10-15 % (it is an approximation, K_A = 0.60 vs exact 0.685 for NACA 4-digit)

experiments.validates: the cantilever bending-moment sum of Calculator.statical_analysis (Ms_n / Ms_t) and the bending stress stress_norm = M*y/I; deflection_flap_m / slope_flap_rad for a future deflection solver
experiments.conditions: constant section NACA 0012 solid c = 0.1 m, E = 70 GPa, clamped at r0 = 0.1 m, free at R = 1 m; loads in the CSV header (uniform 100 N/m, linear 0..200 N/m, tip load 50 N)
experiments.source: closed-form Euler-Bernoulli cantilever (Roark's Formulas for Stress and Strain, 7th ed., Table 8.1), re-derived and verified by numerical integration in extraction/make_reference.py

experiments.validates: the centrifugal force/stress loop of Calculator.statical_analysis (dFc, stress_cent) and the blade mass
experiments.conditions: 600 rpm, rho = 2700 kg/m3, r0 = 0.1 m, R = 1 m; C1 uniform NACA0012 c = 0.1 m; C2 NACA0012 solid with chord linear 0.15 -> 0.05 m
experiments.source: exact integrals F = rho omega^2 int A r dr (uniform bar: sigma = rho omega^2 (R^2 - r^2)/2), extraction/make_reference.py

sources.citation: Chen, H., Yu, W., Capellaro, M. (2010). A critical assessment of computer tools for calculating composite wind turbine blade properties. Wind Energy 13(6):497-516.
Drela, M. Area and Bending Inertia of Airfoil Sections. MIT 16.01 Unified Engineering course notes, Fall 2005 (MIT OpenCourseWare).
Abbott, I.H., von Doenhoff, A.E. (1959). Theory of Wing Sections. Dover. Section 6.4 (NACA four-digit sections: thickness distribution and mean line; thickness applied normal to the mean line).
Young, W.C., Budynas, R.G. (2002). Roark's Formulas for Stress and Strain, 7th ed. McGraw-Hill. Table 8.1 (cantilever beams), Table A.1 (section properties), Table 10.7 (torsion).
Megson, T.H.G. Aircraft Structures for Engineering Students (any ed.), chapter on torsion of closed thin-walled sections (Bredt-Batho J = 4 A^2 t / S).
Drela, M. XFOIL 6.x, BEND command (area, centroid, solid and thin-skin bending inertias). Repository binary xfoil_executables/xfoil; outputs in extraction/xfoil_bend/.

notes: No measured data: this case checks the section-property, moment, stress and centrifugal routines exactly. Frame of section_properties.csv: x chord-wise from the LE to the TE, y normal to the chord to the suction side; Ix = int (y-yc)^2 dA is the FLAPWISE inertia (the program's Ix at blade angle 0), Iy = int (x-xc)^2 dA the edgewise one. The program's rotor-frame transform (to_rotor_frame, X = -x cos b - y sin b, Y = +-(x sin b - y cos b)) at blade angle 0 only mirrors the axes, which leaves Ix, Iy unchanged (wind turbine: both axes flip, Ixy unchanged; propeller: only X flips, Ixy changes sign) - use the theta=0 rows, or the rotation formulas in the CSV header, for other angles. Hollow rows: the wall is the exact inward normal offset of the outline by wall_m (the region within wall_m of the outline), computed with GEOS (shapely) - near a sharp trailing edge the two offset curves meet and the TE wedge is solid, as in a real shell. Known effects seen when the program (state of 2026-10-18) was run on these rows: solid rows agree to ~2e-4 (= the discretisation of the 161-point .dat files, see *_datfile_rel_err); hollow rows agree to <0.3 % for symmetric sections, circle tube A +0.1..+0.8 %, Iy +0.2..+1.2 % (wall 2-10 mm on R = 50 mm: points near the left/right extremes are dropped by the local-thickness criterion of generate_hollow_foil) and NACA 4412/4415 thin walls (2-5 mm on 1 m chord) A -1.3..-2.6 %, Iy -2.7..-5.2 %; the blade-like section needs points along its straight edges (the file has them). XFOIL's own NACA generator adds the thickness vertically (not normal to the camber line): A, xc and Iy of its NACA 4412 equal those of 0012; the NACA definition gives A +0.35 % and Iy +0.7 % for 4412 - the xfoil_* columns are therefore computed on the .dat files of this case.
